Definition: a hemming in, i.e. (objectively) a mound (of siege), or (subjectively) a rampart (of protection), (abstractly) fortification
BiblicalUsage: The fenced cities of Judah included Zorah and Aijalon and Hebron, and Isaiah says God will lay siege against Jerusalem with a mount and raise forts against her. The word is the siege mound or the rampart itself, the hemming in of a city.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that a siege work is a warning in stone: the same mound that protects a city can be raised against it, and only the Lord is a defence that cannot be turned.
